metadata.content: Michael Carrick future: Man Utd head coach position increasingly in doubt but no final decision made | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Michael Carrick future: Man Utd head coach position increasingly in doubt but no final decision made Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick's position under increasing threat but no final decision made despite worst-ever Premier League start and dropping into relegation zone with Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa By Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett and Danyal Khan Monday 9 November 2026 23:15, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane says under-pressure Man Utd boss Michael Carrick 'talks a lot but doesn't say much' and needs to 'get moving' on improving the team after watching his former side earn a late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, but Sky Sports News has been told as yet, no final decision has been taken about his future. As reported earlier on Monday, the club is carrying out a full review of the team's performance so far this season, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, with a plan for a decision to be made before the end of this international break. Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around. messages.text: Sabalenka starts pursuit of WTA Finals title with opening win

metadata.summary: Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva was also victorious in her Group 2 opener on Monday.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka battles past Karolina Muchova in her opening match at Indian Wells | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka battles past Karolina Muchova in her opening match at Indian Wells Aryna Sabalenka won her Group 2 opener against Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva made light work of Elina Svitolina in a 6-4 6-0 triumph; watch the WTA Finals from Indian Wells this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 10 November 2026 00:02, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aryna Sabalenka against Karolina Muchova from the WTA Finals. Aryna Sabalenka got off to a winning start at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, battling past Karolina Muchova 7-6 (7-2) 7-5, while Mirra Andreeva was also victorious in her Group 2 opener on Monday. A two-time beaten finalist in the WTA Finals - including going down last year to Elena Rybakina, who stole her No 1 ranking this season - Sabalenka is looking to win the tournament for the first time. Rybakina's late withdrawal due to a viral illness and fatigue aids Sabalenka's hopes, as does her opening victory over Wimbledon finalist Muchova, who made her sweat for it in a hugely-absorbing contest that ran six minutes shy of two hours. metadata.summary: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has not been named in the FIFPRO World 11.
metadata.content: FIFPRO World 11: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane not voted by fellow professionals to be named in team of the year | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content FIFPRO World 11: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane not voted by fellow professionals to be named in team of the year Harry Kane becomes the first Ballon d'Or winner to not be named in the FIFPRO World 11 after claiming the award; England team-mate Jude Bellingham is included; seven WSL stars have made the Women's FIFPRO World 11 Callum Bishop Football Journalist Monday 9 November 2026 17:15, UK Image: England captain Harry Kane was not named in the FIFPRO World 11 despite winning the Ballon d'Or Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has not been named in the FIFPRO World 11. Over 18,000 professional footballers have chosen their best men's team, with the final 11 being chosen from a group of 26 selected finalists. Kane, who won the Ballon d'Or ahead of Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe by one of the smallest margins in history, was among the 26 finalists but did not make the final team. Mbappe, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami's Lionel Messi were named in a Kane-less front four, which also excluded Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Olise. messages.text: England duo ruled out of rest of Nations Championship

metadata.summary: England will be without Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the remainder of their Nations Championship campaign after both players were ruled out due to injury.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry ruled out of rest of tournament | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: England's Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry ruled out of rest of tournament Steve Borthwick's side have been hit by a raft of injuries ahead of their Nations Championship clash against Japan; Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry have been ruled out of the autumn series Monday 9 November 2026 18:38, UK Image: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has been ruled out of England's Nations Championship campaign England will be without Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the remainder of their Nations Championship campaign after both players were ruled out due to injury. It comes as Steve Borthwick's side has been hit with a series of injuries ahead of their clash against Japan on Saturday. Seb Atkinson, who came off in the second-half of England's 45-22 win against Australia, is set to miss the match with a hip injury, along with Ollie Chessum (shoulder) and George Furbank (groin). messages.text: Norris: McLaren still not at championship level

metadata.summary: Lando Norris believes McLaren are "not at the level to fight for a world championship" despite his dominant win in mixed conditions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris says McLaren are still not at the level to fight for world championship in 2027 despite Sao Paulo Grand Prix win | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lando Norris says McLaren are still not at the level to fight for world championship in 2027 despite Sao Paulo Grand Prix win Lando Norris won a rain-affected Sao Paulo Grand Prix by nearly 15 seconds but he feels McLaren still have work to do ahead of 2027 to fight for the world title again; watch every session of the Las Vegas Grand Prix from November 20-22, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Monday 9 November 2026 13:07, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict on a wet Sao Paulo GP, where Lando Norris won, Max Verstappen fought from the back and Mercedes secured the constructors' title Lando Norris believes McLaren are "not at the level to fight for a world championship" despite his dominant win in mixed conditions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Norris converted pole position into victory for the third time this season as McLaren's upgrades in Brazil, including new wings and floor components, gave them immediate performance. But, Norris feels he benefitted from mistakes, including Kimi Antonelli who spun when leading the race, and George Russell who spun in the pit lane, which exacerbated his 15-second winning margin over Red Bull's Max Verstappen. messages.text: Fleming turns to uncapped spinner amid big calls for first Test series as England coach

metadata.summary: England have called up uncapped left-arm finger spinner Liam Patterson-White for this winter's three-Test series in South Africa, while Shoaib Bashir has dropped down to the Lions squad.
metadata.content: England Test squad for South Africa: Uncapped spinner Liam Patterson-White called up and Jacob Bethell returns | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Test squad for South Africa: Uncapped spinner Liam Patterson-White called up and Jacob Bethell returns England selectors name a 15-player squad for the three-Test series away to South Africa with uncapped spinner Liam Patterson-White earning a call-up; Shoaib Bashir dropped to Lions squad; Jacob Bethell returns to the Test squad following his knee injury during the summer Monday 9 November 2026 13:31, UK England have called up uncapped left-arm finger spinner Liam Patterson-White for this winter's three-Test series in South Africa, while Shoaib Bashir has dropped down to the Lions squad. All-rounder Patterson-White helped Nottinghamshire win the Championship title in 2025 by taking 26 wickets and scoring 540 runs in 11 appearances, and then claimed 42 wickets and scored 474 runs in 14 appearances last season. Jacob Bethell did not feature in August and September's 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to a knee problem that required surgery, but he is back to add to England's batting options for a tour that is live in full on Sky Sports across December and January in what will be Stephen Fleming's first series as head coach. messages.text: England pave way for Carse return

metadata.summary: England have left the door open for Brydon Carse to return to the Test side after the fast bowler was called up to the 15-man Lions squad for their tour of South Africa.
metadata.content: Brydon Carse: England pave way for fast bowler's Test return ahead of South Africa series and will continue to 'invest' in Shoaib Bashir | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Brydon Carse: England pave way for fast bowler's Test return ahead of South Africa series and will continue to 'invest' in Shoaib Bashir Brydon Carse was included in England Lions' 15-man squad for their upcoming tour of South Africa and could be in line for a Test return; spinner Shoaib Bashir drops out of senior red ball squad; watch England's three-Test series vs South Africa live on Sky Sports Monday 9 November 2026 17:29, UK Image: Brydon Carse could return to play for England during their Test series against South Africa England have left the door open for Brydon Carse to return to the Test side after the fast bowler was called up to the 15-man Lions squad for their tour of South Africa. The 31-year-old was dropped from the Test squad midway through their summer series against Pakistan after he was arrested and later 'de-arrested' following an incident outside a Derby nightclub in August . Derbyshire police ended their investigation into the incident in September, but Carse was later charged by the Cricket Regulator and is yet to learn his fate. metadata.content: Oscar Piastri: McLaren driver splits from Mark Webber management after Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Oscar Piastri: McLaren driver splits from Mark Webber management after Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have parted ways with immediate effect; Webber is a former Red Bull and Williams driver and, like Piastri, has won nine Formula 1 races; the pair had been together since 2019 when Piastri was coming up the junior single-seater ranks Monday 9 November 2026 11:09, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Oscar Piastri has split from his management team, led by former Red Bull driver and nine-time Formula 1 winner Mark Webber and his partner Ann Webber. Mark Webber started working with Piastri in 2019 before the latter made his Formula 1 debut in 2023 for McLaren after winning the Formula 3 and Formula 2 titles in consecutive seasons. The news was confirmed after another disappointing weekend for Piastri where he finished sixth, 56 seconds behind team-mate and race-winner Lando Norris.
